## Proof

**Theorem.** Let $E_1, E_2$ be elliptic curves over a number field $k$ that are $k$-isogenous. Let $v$ be a finite place of $k$ of good reduction. Then the reductions $(E_1)_v$ and $(E_2)_v$ are isogenous over the residue field $\mathbb{F}_v$.

**Proof.**

Let $\varphi: E_1 \to E_2$ be a $k$-isogeny of degree $n$, and let $\hat\varphi: E_2 \to E_1$ be the dual isogeny, so that
$$\hat\varphi \circ \varphi = [n]_{E_1}, \qquad \varphi \circ \hat\varphi = [n]_{E_2}.$$

**Step 0 (Good reduction is shared).** Since $E_1$ and $E_2$ are $k$-isogenous, their $\ell$-adic Tate modules $T_\ell(E_1)$ and $T_\ell(E_2)$ are isomorphic as $G_k$-representations (for any $\ell$). By the Néron–Ogg–Shafarevich criterion, $E_i$ has good reduction at $v$ if and only if $T_\ell(E_i)$ is unramified at $v$ (for $\ell \neq \operatorname{char}(\mathbb{F}_v)$). Hence $E_1$ and $E_2$ have good reduction at exactly the same places. In particular, $v$ being a place of good reduction means both $E_1$ and $E_2$ have good reduction at $v$.

**Step 1 (Extension to Néron models).** Let $\mathcal{O}_v$ be the ring of integers of the completion $k_v$, with residue field $\mathbb{F}_v$. Let $\mathcal{N}(E_i)$ denote the Néron model of $E_i$ over $\operatorname{Spec}(\mathcal{O}_v)$. By the universal property of Néron models, the isogeny $\varphi$ extends uniquely to a homomorphism of smooth group schemes
$$\Phi: \mathcal{N}(E_1) \longrightarrow \mathcal{N}(E_2),$$
and likewise $\hat\varphi$ extends to $\hat\Phi: \mathcal{N}(E_2) \to \mathcal{N}(E_1)$. The identities $\hat\varphi \circ \varphi = [n]_{E_1}$ and $\varphi \circ \hat\varphi = [n]_{E_2}$ extend (by uniqueness) to
$$\hat\Phi \circ \Phi = [n]_{\mathcal{N}(E_1)}, \qquad \Phi \circ \hat\Phi = [n]_{\mathcal{N}(E_2)}.$$

**Step 2 (Reduction to the special fiber).** Since $E_1$ and $E_2$ have good reduction at $v$, the Néron models $\mathcal{N}(E_i)$ are abelian schemes over $\operatorname{Spec}(\mathcal{O}_v)$, and their special fibers are the reduced elliptic curves $(E_i)_{v}$ over $\mathbb{F}_v$. Restricting the identity $\hat\Phi \circ \Phi = [n]_{\mathcal{N}(E_1)}$ to the special fiber gives
$$\hat\varphi_v \circ \varphi_v = [n]_{(E_1)_v},$$
where $\varphi_v : (E_1)_v \to (E_2)_v$ and $\hat\varphi_v : (E_2)_v \to (E_1)_v$ are the reductions of $\varphi$ and $\hat\varphi$ modulo $v$.

**Step 3 ($[n]$ on an elliptic curve is always an isogeny).** The multiplication-by-$n$ map $[n]_{(E_1)_v}$ on the elliptic curve $(E_1)_v / \mathbb{F}_v$ is a finite morphism of degree $n^2$, regardless of the characteristic of $\mathbb{F}_v$. (In characteristic $p \mid n$, the map $[p]$ may be purely inseparable, but it is still a finite surjective endomorphism of degree $p^2$.) In particular, $[n]_{(E_1)_v}$ is an isogeny: it is finite and surjective.

**Step 4 ($\varphi_v$ is finite, hence an isogeny).** Since $\hat\varphi_v \circ \varphi_v = [n]_{(E_1)_v}$ is a finite morphism, $\varphi_v$ must be finite. Indeed, if $\ker(\varphi_v)$ had positive dimension, then $\ker(\hat\varphi_v \circ \varphi_v) \supseteq \ker(\varphi_v)$ would also have positive dimension, contradicting the finiteness of $[n]_{(E_1)_v}$.

A finite homomorphism $\varphi_v: (E_1)_v \to (E_2)_v$ between elliptic curves is an isogeny: its image is an abelian subvariety of $(E_2)_v$, hence either $\{0\}$ or $(E_2)_v$ (since $(E_2)_v$ is one-dimensional). Since $\varphi_v$ is finite and $(E_1)_v$ is one-dimensional, the image cannot be $\{0\}$; thus $\varphi_v$ is surjective. Being a surjective finite homomorphism, $\varphi_v$ is an isogeny.

**Conclusion.** The reduction $\varphi_v : (E_1)_v \to (E_2)_v$ is an isogeny over $\mathbb{F}_v$. Therefore, the reduced curves $(E_1)_v$ and $(E_2)_v$ are isogenous over the residue field. $\blacksquare$

**Remark.** The argument uses only that $[n]$ on an elliptic curve is always an isogeny (in every characteristic) and the Néron mapping property, so it works uniformly whether or not $\operatorname{char}(\mathbb{F}_v)$ divides the degree $n$. The same proof applies to abelian varieties of arbitrary dimension.
